summary: WebSocket permessage-deflate corruption behind edge throttling results in garbled final tokens and missing finish_reason
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NotePad AI reports intermittent corrupted final output when using the WebSocket streaming endpoint with permessage-deflate enabled and high burst traffic. Symptoms: final tokens are garbled (non-UTF8 glyphs or stray control characters) and the SDK client never receives the closing metadata (finish_reason/stop sequence). This causes client-side JSON parsing failures and perceived truncated responses.

Impact:
- Affected customer: NotePad AI (dedicated capacity).
- Intermittent but reproducible during high-concurrency bursts when edge rate-limiter or CDN returns 429s mid-stream.
- Users see corrupted trailing text or incomplete JSON, downstream UIs show partial replies and retry loops.

Environment:
- prod - us-east-1, dedicated pool id: dp-46b3
- Client: NotePad AI proprietary SDK v1.4 with permessage-deflate negotiated on WS handshake
- Model: redwood-7b-v1, streaming mode, chunk_size ~512 tokens

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Open WebSocket to wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams with Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate; client_id header set.
2) Start a long-running generation (30s+) that yields multiple frames across minutes.
3) Simulate burst traffic (20 concurrent streams) from the same customer IP to trigger edge rate-limiter.
4) When edge returns a 429 or injects a compressed short-circuit (observed in traces), the client receives a final compressed frame that appears truncated to the decompressor.

Observed behavior:
- Last message body contains high-bit garbage (e.g. "\u0000\ufffd\ufffd\ufffd") or stray bytes appended to valid tokens.
- SDK logs show decompression error or silently emits replacement characters and then never receives the JSON finish object containing finish_reason and metadata.
- Server-side traces show the model emitted the final choice and finish metadata, but those bytes do not successfully reach the client.

Expected behavior:
- Permessage-deflate should yield a well-formed final decompressed payload; finish_reason metadata should be delivered in a separate control/data event as documented.

Recent logs / snippets (sanitized):
- Edge trace (edge-rt-12487): 2026-03-10T18:04:22Z POST->WS burst -> rate-limit 429 injected mid-stream; downstream forwarded partial compressed frame, then RST_STREAM.
- Proxy logs (proxy-2b): 2026-03-10T18:04:23Z upstream closed while inflating message: zlib: unexpected EOF
- Serving runtime: 2026-03-10T18:04:23Z choice_complete id=ch_6a9ff finish_reason=stop metadata_sent=true
- Client SDK (NotePad AI): 2026-03-10T18:04:23Z decompressor error: "invalid stored block lengths"; emitted replacement chars and failed JSON parse

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support instructed customer to disable permessage-deflate on their WS handshake (client-side) and route via the same IP with lower concurrency. After disabling compression the customer reported stable, untampered final payloads.

Next steps (in-progress):
- Reproduce in-house using the customer's workload simulator with permessage-deflate and an Edge test harness to inject 429 mid-frame.
- Capture PCAP and ZLIB traces for a failing case.
- Patch edge proxy to avoid returning HTTP 429 mid-compressed-fragment (ensure backpressure signals occur between messages rather than during compressed data blocks).

Notes on risk and scope:
- Root cause appears to be interaction between edge rate-limiter and streaming compressed frames: when the edge interrupts a compressed message the decompressor on the client sees corrupted suffix bytes. This is not strictly a zlib bug but a transport interruption scenario that the stack must handle (either flush/complete frames or close with a clear protocol-level error before truncating).
- Affects customers using permessage-deflate over WebSocket. Not triggered on SSE or uncompressed WS frames.
comments: 2026-03-10 19:02 - Emma Chen: Opened after customer provided request traces and SDK logs. Customer reproduces reliably when their load generator ramps concurrently to 20+ streams. They reported disabling permessage-deflate temporarily fixed the issue.

2026-03-10 20:15 - Raj Patel: Confirmed we can reproduce a zlib EOF when we inject an upstream RST during an ongoing compressed frame. Created a minimal repro harness and filed INT-412 to track edge proxy change.

2026-03-11 09:32 - SRE (Marta Gomez): Collected pcap + zlib raw stream from repro run (s3://redwood-support/artifacts/SUP-204842/pcap.tar.gz). Observed the same truncated deflate block and decompressor error on client-side.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 - Hypothesis: Edge rate-limiter currently returns a 429 with a short response body while a compressed WS message is mid-stream; the proxy does not signal an application-level close, resulting in truncated compressed blocks reaching the client decompress path.

Edge proxy component (edge-proxy v2.4.1) uses streaming-chunk forwarding; on high load it attempts opportunistic early 429 and can close TCP connection mid-message. Need to ensure 429 responses are delivered only between compressed message boundaries or convert to a higher-level control frame.

Repro notes: Reproducer uses ws-client with permessage-deflate, sends 30s generation. Reproducer injection: close server->client socket after 70% of compressed frame bytes forwarded. Client zlib error matches customer logs.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Short-term: Edge and proxy teams applied a guard to avoid injecting 429 while a compressed message is in-flight; instead the edge now marks session for graceful throttling and sends a TCP FIN after the current message completes where possible.

2026-03-12 - Medium-term: Implement detection to disable permessage-deflate negotiation on customer-dedicated pools if edge-conditions cannot guarantee message boundary safety. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/781 (in review).
Follow-up: Add automated integration test in CI to simulate mid-frame interruptions and assert that client receives explicit protocol close or intact frames (ticket INT-412).
